t:
(a) In General.—The Secretary may make grants to a State to assist the State in conforming to the minimum standards set forth in this title. 
    (b) Authorization of Appropriations.—There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary for each of the fiscal years 2005 through 2009 such sums as may be necessary to carry out this title.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a State, an outside party, is involved with the Secretary. But the State is only a grant recipient, and the definition excludes grants and applications for them from participation. The rest of the section just authorizes appropriations, with no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue.
fable.s: The Secretary may make grants to a State to assist the State in conforming to the minimum standards set forth in this title.

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the Secretary to provide grants to states. The definition explicitly states that participation 'does not include applications for benefits or grants.' While states are outside the federal government, the act of receiving a grant is not considered participation in the decision-making process under this definition. There is no requirement for consultation, public comment, or advisory boards involving outside parties in this specific text.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary may make grants to a State to assist the State in conforming to the minimum standards set forth in this title.

opus.w: The section only authorizes the Secretary to give grants to States and authorizes funding for them. Grants and grant applications are expressly excluded from the definition of participation. A State appears in the text, but it receives money; it does not take part in any federal decision through consultation, a hearing, a comment period, an advisory body, or a right to sue.
opus.s: The Secretary may make grants to a State to assist the State in conforming to the minimum standards set forth in this title.
opus.b: Someone might read this as participation because it involves a State and the Secretary. That reading fails. The section only lets the Secretary give grants to States and authorizes the money for them. Grants are expressly excluded from the definition, and nothing here requires consulting outsiders, a comment period, a hearing, rulemaking, or a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section authorizes the Secretary to make grants to States. The definition explicitly excludes 'applications for benefits or grants' from the scope of participation. While States are outside entities, the mechanism described is financial assistance rather than consultation, coordination, or advisory input into a federal decision.
qwen_chat.s: (a) In General.—The Secretary may make grants to a State to assist the State in conforming to the minimum standards set forth in this title.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the grants are given to States (outside entities), this constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly states: "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." The section describes the authority to make grants, which falls squarely into this exclusion. The interaction is a funding mechanism, not a consultative process or advisory role in decision-making.
